component.name: FujiNet Go Adam
component.summary: Self-contained Coleco ADAM with built-in FujiNet

description.p: A Coleco ADAM (and ColecoVision) with FujiNet built in: mount disk and data-pack images from TNFS servers or the local SD folder, configure everything through the embedded FujiNet web UI, and play with automatic gamepad support. For developers it includes a full debugger with breakpoints, stepping, instruction history, EOS/OS7 symbols, and live VDP table viewers.

screenshot.caption: A Coleco ADAM running with FujiNet built in

description.p: Fixes N: opens on AdamNet carrying the padding that follows the device spec. The client libraries send a fixed-size command block, so the URL arrives with the rest of the field after it; the runtime now stops at the end of the string, as every other bus does. A protocol that reads the device spec byte for byte — the new CALENDAR, GCAL and ICAL protocols do — saw the padding as part of the URL, so a GCAL day view was fetched as a calendar named after its own date and came back empty.

The bundled FujiNet runtime moves up to the current firmware. The web UI gains an optional global password and an SD card file manager; N: gains the CALENDAR, GCAL and ICAL protocols; the CONFIG slot-assignment screen shows the right filenames again; opening an AdamNet network connection no longer crashes on a null device; and a zero-length app key write clears the key instead of failing.
The runtime also builds again on systems that ship Mbed TLS 4.x, which no longer carries the legacy crypto headers it needs.

The debugger's VDP tab gains a VRAM hex editor (read and poke bytes directly, addresses wrap at 16K), a decoded view of the registers and the table addresses each mode is actually fetching from, and a redrawn palette strip with a separate, labeled square per color.
The Linux release now ships .deb/.rpm/.tar.gz packages (via CPack) alongside the flatpaks, matching the sibling CoCo and Apple II desktop apps' own release process.

Fixes the FujiNet Configuration window being unreachable when another FujiNet-family process on the machine already held the web admin's port. It now binds a random free port each run instead of a fixed one.
Fixes the OneDrive and Google Drive Authorize buttons in the FujiNet configuration page, which silently did nothing: they now open in the system browser, which OAuth requires anyway.
macOS: the app now ships its own icon in the Dock, Finder and Launchpad instead of the generic bundle icon.

Removes a multi-second freeze while loading. When the drive missed a request it was left to time out, stalling the machine for five seconds before anything retried; the request is now re-sent promptly.
Windows: FujiNet now starts. The shipped runtime library pulled in two libraries that were not part of the download, so it failed to load and the ADAM booted to SmartWriter with no FujiNet at all.

Fixes disk and data-pack loading: a drive now reports itself busy while it positions on a block and serves the data when the guest asks again, as the hardware does. Titles whose loaders rely on that exchange — Donkey Kong Super Game among them — previously stopped part-way and drew their play screen with the wrong graphics mode and colours.
Fixes a duplicate block problem in the ADAMnet-over-IP transport that could corrupt block reads from FujiNet.
FujiNet now runs on Windows as well, the native debugger is available in every frontend, and the macOS build gained the standard application, Window and Settings menus.
